Материал содержит многочисленные иллюстрации, демонстрирующие категории плотности.

educational_units.title: Breast Density Definition
educational_units.description: Definition of breast density as the relative proportion of breast parenchyma to fat.
educational_units.evidence: Breast density is defined as the relative proportion of breast parenchyma to fat...

educational_units.title: BI-RADS Breast Density Categories
educational_units.description: The four categories of breast density (A, B, C, D) and their descriptions, indicating mammography sensitivity.
educational_units.evidence: Table 1 & 2, 'There are four categories of breast density...'

educational_units.title: Dense vs. Non-Dense Breasts
educational_units.description: Distinction between 'dense' (categories C, D) and 'non-dense' (categories A, B) breasts.
educational_units.evidence: People with heterogeneously dense or extremely dense breasts are considered to have dense breasts...

educational_units.title: FDA Legislation on Breast Density Reporting
educational_units.description: Requirement by FDA for reporting breast density as of September 2024, with an update in July 2025 for singular phrasing.
educational_units.evidence: Reporting breast density is required by Food and Drug Administration (FDA) legislation as of September 2024.

factual_anchors.value: FDA Legislation on Breast Density Reporting

educational_units.title: Significance of Breast Density
educational_units.description: Breast density is significant for mammographic accuracy (masking effect) and breast cancer risk.
educational_units.evidence: Breast density is significant for two reasons: mammographic accuracy and breast cancer risk.

educational_units.title: Masking Effect
educational_units.description: Explanation of how dense fibroglandular tissue can obscure small masses, reducing mammography sensitivity.
educational_units.evidence: The impact of breast density on mammographic accuracy is due to the masking effect of dense fibro-glandular tissue.

educational_units.title: Breast Cancer Risk by Density Category
educational_units.description: Increased inherent risk for developing breast cancer with heterogeneously dense and extremely dense breasts, quantified by odds ratios.
educational_units.evidence: Compared to the breasts of women with scattered fibroglandular tissue, the odds ratio of breast cancer is 0.6 for almost entirely fatty. 1.4 for heterogeneously dense, and 1.6 for extremely dense breasts [12].

factual_anchors.value: Breast Cancer Risk by Density Category

educational_units.title: Evolution of Breast Density Classification
educational_units.description: Shift in classification from percentage of dense tissue to assessment based on likelihood of obscuring cancer (BI-RADS 5th Edition and v2025).
educational_units.evidence: With the BI-RADS 5th Edition, the classification of breast density changed from an evaluation of the percentage of dense tissue to an assessment based on the likelihood that overlying tissue may obscure a cancer.

educational_units.title: Factors Affecting Breast Density Variability
educational_units.description: Factors such as weight changes, estrogen replacement therapy, and menopause can cause breast density to vary year to year.
educational_units.evidence: Breast density can be variable from year to year, depending on multiple factors such as weight gain or loss, estrogen replacement therapy, menopause, etc.

educational_units.title: Mammography Mass Characteristics
educational_units.description: Classification of masses by shape (oval, lobulated, round, irregular), margin (circumscribed, obscured, indistinct, spiculated), and density (fat-containing, low, equal, high).

educational_units.title: Mammography Calcification Characteristics
educational_units.description: Classification of calcifications by morphology (typically benign, suspicious) and distribution (diffuse, regional, grouped, linear, segmental).

educational_units.title: Other Mammography Findings
educational_units.description: Categories for architectural distortion, asymmetries, lymph nodes, skin lesions, and dilated ducts.
educational_units.evidence: Table 1, Sections C, D, E, F, G.

educational_units.title: Associated Features and Special Cases
educational_units.description: Associated features (skin/nipple retraction, thickening) and special cases (gynecomastia, implants, mastectomy) in mammography.

educational_units.title: Location of Finding Parameters
educational_units.description: Parameters for describing the location of a finding: laterality, location in breast, depth and/or distance from the nipple.

educational_units.title: Impact of Technology on Mammography Sensitivity
educational_units.description: Digital mammography and DBT significantly improved sensitivity in women with dense breasts by reducing the masking effect, with specific detection rates.
educational_units.evidence: In the DMIST trial, the sensitivity of mammography in women with dense breasts increased from 55% with film mammography to 70% with digital mammography [10].

factual_anchors.value: Impact of Technology on Mammography Sensitivity
